fixes.explanation: Right, friend! Jesus says, “Carry no purse or bag or sandals.” That's a short packing list, and it's a short one. Imagine the stares at the front door of the first house.

Yes, friend. In Luke 10:7 Jesus says, “Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered.” Then He adds, “Do not move around from house to house.” So where they're welcomed is where they settle in. No house-hopping.

Right, baker! Jesus says, “Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’” There's something to do and something to say. Both are in the same verse, and I'd say that's a full day's work.

That's the word, baker! Jesus says those cities “…would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.” He says Tyre and Sidon would have done it. Chorazin and Bethsaida had the miracles performed in them, so His words to them are heavy.

I get the pull of that one, friend, but it isn't what Jesus says. He says Tyre and Sidon “…would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.” Rebelled is a different word from repented. Repented is the one in the verse.
It's the opposite, baker. Luke 10:17 says, “The seventy-two returned with joy…” Joy is how the text says they came back. Then they tell Jesus, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”

Jesus does say it, friend. In Luke 10:19 He tells them, “Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy.” He says He has given it to them, and then adds, “Nothing will harm you.” So this one is True.

Close in sound, baker, but not what Jesus says. He says “…many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it…” Judges and elders aren't mentioned there. The ones He names are prophets and kings.
